title: Chapter 12: Files, NIO, Date-Time, Regex, and Serialization
description: Cross file, text, time, and serialization boundaries explicitly. Learners constrain resolved paths to an approved root, stream bytes and characters with declared UTF-8 encoding, select correct java.time types and inject Clock, design and test bounded regular expressions, and version serialization schemas without exposing implementation objects or enabling native-deserialization attacks.

exercises.title: Chapter 12 implementation lab: courseCode
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `courseCode`. Accept exactly two uppercase ASCII letters, a hyphen, and four digits. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Use whole-input matching and ASCII letters/digits, not a substring search.
hints: Require the pattern to match the whole string, not merely be contained in it: two uppercase ASCII letters, a hyphen, then exactly four digits.
Test a lowercase code, an extra prefix or suffix, the wrong digit count, and the exact minimum-length boundary before submitting.

exercises.title: Whole-region grammar
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Repair the regex check so it validates the entire input region instead of finding a matching substring inside `prefix JV-0021`, and the program writes exactly `false`. Keep the same compiled pattern and explain why matches() versus find() changes the outcome, rather than hard-coding the print statement. Output tests verify the printed result; confirming whole-input validation actually happens requires reading the source.
hints: The requirement validates the entire input, not a matching substring.

exercises.title: Portfolio checkpoint: session overlap scheduler
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement SessionScheduler.run(String input) as the pure decision core behind the Study Group Web App project, using java.time.LocalDateTime for every timestamp. Each nonblank trimmed line is one command; blank lines are skipped and produce no output line. SCHEDULE|member|groupId|start|durationMinutes requires member and groupId to match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,20}, start to parse as an ISO-8601 local date-time such as 2024-03-10T10:00, and durationMinutes to be a positive integer; the session's interval is [start, start+durationMinutes). If this interval intersects any other interval already scheduled for the same member (regardless of group), where two half-open intervals intersect exactly when each one's start is strictly before the other's end, print CONFLICT without recording it; a malformed line prints ERROR; otherwise record it and print OK. CANCEL|member|groupId|start prints OK and removes the session only if one was recorded for exactly that member, groupId, and start; otherwise ERROR. UPCOMING|member|now (now also an ISO-8601 local date-time) prints every currently recorded session for that member whose start is not before now, sorted chronologically ascending by start, formatted groupId@start separated by semicolons, or EMPTY if none qualify. Output is one line per nonblank input line, joined with \n, no trailing newline. This models only the overlap-detection and listing core; a real study-group app's authentication and reviews are external, ungraded scope.
hints: Back-to-back sessions (one ending exactly when the other starts) do not overlap — the interval is half-open, [start, end).
UPCOMING compares against the given now parameter, never the real system clock, so results stay deterministic.
